set.body:
Found by the PLS Neuro basis-set review on 2026-09-11 and checked numerically by an independent reviewer. Revision a3ee73b.

What the code does: HrfFunctions.scala:70-75 defines spmg1(t) = exp(-t) * (A1 * t^P1 - C * t^P2) with P1 = 5, P2 = 15, A1 = 0.0833 and C = spmg1C = 1.274527e-13.

What SPM does: its canonical, gampdf(t,6,1) - gampdf(t,16,1)/6, expands to exp(-t) * (t^5/120 - t^15/(6*15!)). That is A1 = 1/120 = 0.008333 and C = 1/(6*15!) = 1.2745e-13. C matches SPM exactly; A1 is ten times larger.

Effect: the post-stimulus undershoot is about 0.6% of the peak, with its trough near 17 s, instead of about 8.9% near 15 s. Peak timing barely moves. spmg1Deriv and spmg1SecondDeriv inherit the same constants, so SPMG2/3 shapes differ from SPM's too. Amplitudes compared against SPM, or against fits using another canonical, are not like for like.

The code claims R parity, so fmrihrf's hrf_spmg1 probably carries the same constants. Check it there as well.

Decide: correct A1 to 1/120 here and in fmrihrf, or keep it for parity and document that this canonical is not SPM's, naming it accordingly.
set.title: SPMG1 canonical: peak coefficient A1 = 0.0833 is ten times SPM's 1/120, shrinking the undershoot to 0.6% of peak
